1	\section{Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	We characterized how multi-class annotation errors interact with causal DAG topology: at $K{\geq}3$, exposure and IV can reverse treatment effect signs while five topologies preserve them. ASVs provide a topology-dependent vulnerability ranking; matrix-based corrections are provably ineffective for four covariate topologies (FWL invariance). Practitioners should identify the topology first: for exposure, PPI++ reduces bias from ${\sim}61\%$ to ${<}1\%$ (Table~\ref{tab:e2e-real-cm}); for IV, all tested corrections worsen the estimate. High $F_1$ does not guarantee low causal bias; topology assessment must precede downstream inference.
5	
6	Differential misclassification and proving Conjecture~\ref{conj:monotone} for general $K$ remain open.
7	
8	\section*{Limitations}
9	
10	Our closed-form results assume linear SEMs with proportional effects ($f{=}\lambda g$); sign preservation empirically holds at 97.3\% under non-proportional effects (Table~\ref{tab:proportional_empirical}), but recommendations do not directly extend to nonlinear models (matching, doubly-robust). The framework assumes a known DAG with non-differential misclassification (Appendix~\ref{sec:nondiff_stress}); DAG misspecification under measurement error may compound bias. ASV computation requires gold labels for $C^{-1}$; error propagation under small gold-label budgets ($<$500) and general $K{\geq}3$ envelope monotonicity (Conjecture~\ref{conj:monotone}) remain open.

lines: -When large language model (LLM)-generated annotations feed into causal inference, annotation quality alone is insufficient to assess causal validity; the causal directed acyclic graph (DAG) topology determines whether errors attenuate, amplify, or reverse the treatment effect estimate. We derive bias expressions for seven canonical topologies under $K$-class non-differential misclassification in linear structural equation models and show that $K {\geq} 3$ introduces a structural possibility of sign reversal absent in the binary case. Under proportional effects, five topologies preserve the treatment effect sign under regularity conditions; exposure and instrumental variable (IV) can reverse it. Under empirical LLM confusion matrices, sign reversal is confined to exposure topology. We introduce Annotation Sensitivity Values (ASVs), with proved ($K{=}2$, $K{=}3$ symmetric) and extensively validated (general $K{\geq}3$) monotonicity that yields a vulnerability ranking from IV (maximally fragile) to M-bias (immune), and show that matrix-based corrections are provably ineffective under linear regression for four topologies due to Frisch--Waugh--Lovell invariance. A case study with 10 real LLM confusion matrices confirms: topology-aware correction reduces exposure bias from 61\% to $<$1\%, while topology-blind corrections are provably futile under linear regression for four topologies.
